lead_notes: Four wave-1 branches were merged before any of them was gated, and 6d496b8c's conformance failures then made cargo-ci red on main for every issue at once, blocking completion of five otherwise-finished issues. The protocol 3019eacd rewrote names exactly this: gate after each merge whenever per-merge attribution matters. Gate before merging the next branch from here on.

A backgrounded `codex exec` blocks forever on 'Reading additional input from stdin...' unless stdin is redirected from /dev/null. The 6d496b8c rework sat 17 minutes with a live process, a clean worktree, no commits and 00:00:00 CPU before this was found. It is a harness defect, not a worker failure, and does not count against the rework budget.

surfaced_pitfalls.finding: scripts/assemble-package-selftest.sh passes and covers every criterion, but nothing runs it: no gate, no CI job, and no Rust test invokes it, so the argument contract can regress without any check failing. The repository has both patterns — workflow-contract-selftest.sh runs from a CI step and verify-commit-builds-selftest.sh from a Rust test in crates/jit/tests/scratch_build, while install-jit-selftest.sh, benchmark-session-cost-selftest.sh and generate-shipped-policy-regions-selftest.sh are unwired.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: Closed. The code-review gate independently raised it as blocking, citing the container's REQ-06. 3019eacd kept crates/jit/tests/scratch_build and put merged_tree_gate_verification_tests.rs there to run cargo-ci-selftest.sh from a Rust test, so the wiring precedent was alive rather than about to disappear. Fixed lead-direct at 7e1df315 by adding a module to that same suite; verified passing.
surfaced_pitfalls.criterion_subject: 5367fcba REQ-01..REQ-04 describe behaviour no gate currently observes

surfaced_pitfalls.finding: The worker corrected a now-false CI statement in dev/active/c639cfb5-jit-profiles-complete/c639cfb5-investigation.md, an investigation document owned by a different container, and dropped its line-number citation into the workflow file while doing so.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: Accepted. The brief's REQ-03 sweep reaches that surface and the statement was false after the change; the lost citation pointed at line numbers the edit moved anyway.

surfaced_pitfalls.finding: The merged change failed cargo-ci on main: adding a command surface requires registering it in every conformance suite that enumerates command surfaces, and four were missed — the classifier table in crates/jit/src/main.rs (repaired lead-direct), the row-set equality guard and both end-to-end subprocess bindings in command_exit_code_projection_tests, and the clap-arm probe in failure_probe_coverage_tests.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: Rework dispatched with all four findings named and a constraint forbidding any weakening of the assertions. Rework count 1 of 2.

surfaced_pitfalls.finding: The teardown's drained assertion reads an unreaped zombie as a surviving process, so on a host whose PID 1 never reaps orphans the case could fail spuriously after its 15-second teardown budget. The worker judged the risk low on a virtual-machine runner and kept the strict check because it is the direct evidence for REQ-02.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: Accepted. The failure mode is a bounded failure rather than the unbounded hang the issue exists to remove, and the message distinguishes a live survivor from a zombie by reporting whether the announced port still answers.

surfaced_pitfalls.finding: The test's kill_process_group calls the same nix primitive under the same pid-safety guard as the private helper at crates/jit/src/gate_execution.rs:345, rather than sharing it. The worker named this against @/inv/convention-convergence rather than leaving it silent.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: Accepted. The product helper is private to its module and takes a Child, so an integration test cannot reach it; exporting production API for a test's use is the worse trade. The shared mechanism actually at stake — the guarded conversion that keeps a negation from becoming kill(-1) — is followed and cited.

surfaced_pitfalls.finding: setup_repo now bounds and captures its jit init, which widens the change to all ten tests in the module rather than the foreground case alone.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: Accepted. REQ-03 says every wait the test performs is bounded, and the foreground case's own setup is one of those waits; a second parallel setup helper would have violated @/inv/convention-convergence. All ten tests pass.

surfaced_pitfalls.finding: code-review found read_capture's fs::read_to_string bounded by no deadline, citing the container's REQ-08, while the issue's own REQ-03 says every wait, read and join is bounded.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: Reworked. A regular-file read terminates at EOF so it cannot hang like a pipe, and that argument is why the code looked correct — but the criterion says reads are bounded and this one was not. The worker chose a byte cap over a deadline and explained why the deadline is the illusion: nothing cancels a read already issued, so a deadline bounds the observer while the read runs on.

surfaced_pitfalls.finding: docs/reference/example-config.toml carried team:core, the value the registry moved off, as a third carrier bound by no check.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: Fixed at 7b013c12, one line. Deliberately no check: that file illustrates the configuration format for adopters, so binding it would make every adopter example a carrier of this repository's live state. The worker declined two further edits I had asked for and was right both times — the description matched the file's own no-period convention rather than mirroring the registry, and milestone:2026-q1 illustrates the second half of its own sentence rather than mirroring superseded text.
